clue.text: Ooh! A last request for old Dicky produces absolutely zilch

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or shaky, so the letters before it are reworked into a new order

parts.words: Ooh! A last request for old

explanation.surface: A dying old man named Dicky sighs and makes a final wish, which turns out to be for nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old Dicky' looks like a person, but 'Dicky' is the anagram signal: the 21 letters of 'Ooh! A last request for old' rearrange into the full phrase. 'Sod all' is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod all means nothing, and the square root of zero is still zero, so the phrase is a jokey intensifier for nothing whatsoever.

clue.text: Depression caused by barb?

parts.note: a barb is also a Barbary horse, and the hollow it presses into the ground is a mark left by its foot

explanation.surface: Low mood brought on by a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barb' reads as a hurtful comment, and 'depression' as low spirits; in fact the barb is a breed of horse and the depression is a dent in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's hoof pressed into soft ground leaves a hollow, a literal depression made by the animal.

clue.text: Carol keeps John working hard

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to carol is to sing
john is slang for a toilet, as is lav, short for lavatory

explanation.surface: A woman called Carol supports a man called John, who is putting in long hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' and 'John' look like names; they are a verb and a slang word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaving away means toiling like a slave, i.e. labouring very hard.

clue.text: One's left in dark

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one single thing

explanation.surface: Someone has been abandoned without light.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': one has left placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no lamp or light switched on is in darkness, a near synonym.

clue.text: She makes a mint after promotion

indicators.note: in a down clue, promotion means sent upward, so the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Trebor is a British brand of mints, so a mint can be one of its sweets

explanation.surface: A woman earns a fortune once she is promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a mint' suggests earning a fortune; here the mint is a Trebor sweet, a British confectionery brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a woman's first name, so 'She' stands for any woman bearing it.

clue.text: United fan accepts City finished better

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: Manchester United fans are called the Reds
EC is the postcode for the City of London
over means finished

explanation.surface: A Manchester United supporter takes a City result and feels better about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like Manchester City in a football clue, but it is the City of London postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is better after an illness is well again, healed.

clue.text: Number nine originally wearing gold ring

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: wearing here means held within, so the letter sits inside the ring word

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them

indicators.note: originally means taking just the first letter of nine

explanation.surface: A footballer wearing the number nine shirt also wears a gold ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number nine' looks like a striker; 'Number' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are ordinal numbers, words that give position in a series.

clue.text: Touring Ohio, a lot of very fat musicians

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the shortened word surrounds the abbreviation
a lot of means most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: obese means very fat

explanation.surface: A band of overweight musicians on tour in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the final E of OBESE, leaving OBES, which goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral players are often named after their instruments, so the woodwind instruments stand for the people who play them.

clue.text: See 1
Secret support by party rank and file

parts.note: to back is to support
a do is a party
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Covert backing from the ordinary members of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdoor deal is a clandestine, underhand one, done out of sight.

clue.text: He shifts second piece of computer hardware

parts.note: a printer is a peripheral device for a computer

explanation.surface: A man moves a second device for his computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like moving furniture, but in slang to shift is to go fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner of short races moves very fast, and shift is slang for move quickly.

clue.text: Go like an old Dormobile?

parts.note: a Dormobile was a British make of camper van, now gone
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat

explanation.surface: Head off in the style of a vintage camper van.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dormobile was a 1960s-70s British camper van, so it is a van.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to go suddenly out of sight.

clue.text: Petty dictator can leave department

parts.note: a can is a tin
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A small-time despot is free to walk out of the department.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who behaves like a minor deity, demanding obedience over a small domain, is a self-important petty tyrant.

clue.text: A bargain — had to cut price drastically

definitions.note: used predicatively, as in 'it was a bargain', where the answer can stand

indicators.note: drastically suggests a violent change, so the letters are reshuffled
cut means shortened, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A shop slashed its prices to offer a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims TO to T; HAD, T and PRICE are then rearranged by 'drastically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very cheap indeed, as cheap as soil, is a real bargain.

clue.text: Meteorite that's landed — hear nothing new about it

indicators.note: about means round, so the rearranged letters go round the other pieces
new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
lit is a past tense of light, as in alight: to come down and land

explanation.surface: A space rock has come down, and there is no fresh news about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges HEAR to AERH, which goes 'about' O and LIT; 'it' points back to those pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A stony meteorite, from Greek for air and stone, is a rock that fell from the sky.

clue.text: True? Phone to find out immediately

indicators.note: find out is read as sort out, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Is that true? Ring right away to check.
explanation.definitionFit: Directly after that, at once: a formal synonym for straight away.

clue.text: Begin to face disaster in chat show

indicators.note: to face means placed in front of, so the first piece leads

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: in chat means spoken aloud, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a wreck is a disaster

explanation.surface: A talk show host starts to confront catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chat show' looks like the definition; 'show' alone is it, and 'in chat' signals a sound-alike of WRECK.
explanation.definitionFit: The science fiction television series is a famous show.

clue.text: Poor women invisible and gagged

indicators.note: invisible means not to be seen, so that letter disappears

parts.note: wretched means poor or pitiful

explanation.surface: Destitute women went unseen and were silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gagged' looks like silenced; here it means heaved.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to heave as if about to vomit, the same as to heave dryly.

clue.text: Toy boy outside Long Room

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the toy's name wraps the other piece

parts.note: Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie
to long for is to itch for

explanation.surface: A young lover waits outside the Long Room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' looks like a young lover but is Ken, the doll. The Long Room is a famous room in the Lord's cricket pavilion, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: The place in a house where food is cooked is one of its rooms.

clue.text: Sacked? Is Pellegrini about to drive away?

indicators.note: about here means carried within, so the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: Football gossip: is the Manchester City manager Pellegrini about to be fired?
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel Pellegrini managed Manchester City when this was set; the answer sits inside 'Sacked? Is Pellegrini'.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase off or scatter something, such as doubts or a crowd, is to banish it.

clue.text: Top guy in sport's promotion English

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the sport holds the other pieces

parts.note: sumo is a Japanese wrestling sport
PR, public relations, is promotion

explanation.surface: The boss of a sport's marketing is English.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, a boss or chief.

clue.text: US writer 'put it about' — see, that's beautifully expressed

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: see is pronounced like the letter C

explanation.surface: An American author spread the word: look, that is finely phrased.
explanation.definitionFit: Language that is lyrical and elegant has the quality of verse.

clue.text: Statesman soon gets upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment, means soon

explanation.surface: A politician quickly becomes annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' looks like a politician, but here it is a man of a state, the Gulf state of Oman.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the Gulf nation of Oman is literally a man of that state.

clue.text: Did tramp depart with 'is bundle?

indicators.note: to bundle is to shove things together roughly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: 'is is a dropped-aitch form of his, written as two letters

explanation.surface: A vagrant leaves carrying his bundle of belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' reads as a vagrant noun; with 'Did' it is a verb, to walk wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge or walk wearily is to tramp; the past tense matches 'Did tramp'.

clue.text: One day they'll help

parts.note: a means one
the Ides is a day in the Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: Someday people will lend a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistants are people whose job is to help.

clue.text: Does he stock ecstasy tablets, heroin or a different drug?

parts.note: asking whether he stocks something is asking whether he has it
E is ecstasy, so several tablets are Es
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A buyer asks whether a dealer carries ecstasy, heroin or some other drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The cannabis resin, spelt this way, is another drug besides ecstasy and heroin.

clue.text: Pass degree course in French town

parts.note: to pass away is to die
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree

explanation.surface: Getting through a degree course in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like passing an exam; it means die.
explanation.definitionFit: A Channel port in Normandy, a well-known town in northern France.

clue.text: Beginning to get frisky in pool (I undress and prepare for action)

indicators.note: beginning to means taking just the first letter of the following word
frisky means playful and lively, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Things start to get playful in the swimming pool as someone strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: After G, 'frisky' shuffles the letters of 'in pool' and 'I undress'.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical idiom means to tuck up long robes before running or working, i.e. to get ready for effort.
